links.outcome: Precision on real-world imbalanced data versus synthetic balanced data
links.effect: GPT-4o precision fell from 0.979 on synthetic Test-2 to 0.219 on real-world Test-1. ClinicalBERT precision fell from 0.984 to 0.047. Test-1 membership predicted false positives (GPT-4o OR 239.89).
links.quote: Both ClinicalBERT and GPT-4o exhibited notable declines in precision on TrainVal and Test-1 compared to Test-2.

links.outcome: Benchmark performance on synthetic balanced data versus real-world imbalanced reports
links.effect: Synthetic balanced data gave F1 of 0.966 for GPT-4o and 0.959 for rule-based+GPT-4o. On real-world Test-1, F1 was 0.352 for GPT-4o and 0.780 for rule-based+GPT-4o.
links.quote: A significant performance gap exists between balanced synthetic datasets and imbalanced real-world data.

links.outcome: Comparison of the candidate ensemble against GPT-4o, ClinicalBERT and RoBERTa on the same test data
links.effect: On Test-1, rule-based+GPT-4o had F1 0.780, versus 0.352 for GPT-4o, 0.088 for ClinicalBERT and 0.000 for RoBERTa.
links.quote: In experiment 2, on Test-1, rule-based+GPT-4o (precision=0.696; recall=0.889; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.780) outperformed GPT-4o (precision=0.219; recall=0.889; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.352), ClinicalBERT (precision=0.047; recall=0.667; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.088), and RoBERTa (F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.000).

unlisted_practices: Hybrid rule-based plus LLM ensemble for radiology report laterality error screening
Evaluating on real-world imbalanced data rather than balanced synthetic data

screen.reason: The study develops and retrospectively evaluates an ensemble algorithm (combining rule-based methods and GPT-4o) to detect laterality errors in radiology reports, comparing it against other models and baselines on retrospective datasets without testing a deployment practice.
